title: SMS filtering — DROPPED from release 1
summary: Android cannot block SMS; iPhone-only decided 2026-09-08
description:
DECIDED 2026-09-08: Android SMS is out of release 1. SMS filtering ships on iPhone only. This phase is closed, not deleted — the reasoning matters if it is ever revisited. It has no tasks and none should be created.

WHY — verified by reading android-36 sources in P001(F001)/T002.
android/provider/Telephony.java, verbatim:
"Only the default SMS app (selected by the user in system settings) is able to write to the SMS Provider ... and only the default SMS app receives the SMS_DELIVER_ACTION broadcast"
"Other apps that are not selected as the default SMS app can only read the SMS Provider, but may also be notified when a new SMS arrives by listening for the SMS_RECEIVED_ACTION broadcast, which is a NON-ABORTABLE broadcast"

A non-default app can observe an incoming SMS. It can never block one. Becoming the default SMS app requires handling SMS_DELIVER (BROADCAST_SMS), WAP_PUSH_DELIVER for MMS (BROADCAST_WAP_PUSH), an ACTION_SENDTO activity and a RESPOND_VIA_MESSAGE service — a complete messaging application. Out of proportion to the feature, and the same line iOS draws with TelephonyMessagingKit, already out of scope.

OPTIONS CONSIDERED:
1. iPhone SMS only — CHOSEN.
2. Android observes and warns, cannot block — deferred to idea I001, which records the full reasoning for not doing it now.
3. Build a full messaging app — rejected as out of proportion.

Play policy was NOT the blocker. Caller ID and spam blocking is a permitted exception to the SMS and Call Log permission policy and does not require default-handler status; it needs a Permissions Declaration Form and Google review. But policy would only have granted RECEIVE_SMS, and the framework still makes the broadcast non-abortable — observation only. The limit is technical.

WHAT ANDROID KEEPS: all seven rule types on calls, live, with real control over the outcome (setDisallowCall, setSilenceCall, setSkipCallLog, setSkipNotification). Calls are Android's strong surface and are unaffected.

SIDE EFFECT WORTH NOTING: dropping Android SMS also removes the restricted SMS permission group from release 1, so the Google Play declaration and review are no longer needed at all. Release 1 now has no launch dependency outside our control.
